pageInfo.subtitle: Learn to improvise using modes to create unique colors and moods beyond major and minor.
pageInfo.heroDescription: Modal improvisation moves beyond the major/minor framework to explore the unique character of each mode. Each mode has its own flavor - from the bright dreaminess of Lydian to the dark tension of Phrygian. Learning to improvise modally opens up new emotional and sonic territory that transforms your soloing.

items.text: Each mode has a characteristic note that defines its sound
Emphasize the characteristic note to establish the modal flavor
Use drone notes or vamps (not full progressions) to establish modes
Avoid notes that pull toward major or minor resolution

exercises.title: Dorian Modal Vamp
exercises.description: Improvise over a Dm7 vamp (one chord) using D Dorian mode (D-E-F-G-A-B-C). The characteristic note is B natural (the major 6th over a minor chord). Emphasize this note to create the Dorian sound heard in Santana, Miles Davis, and many funk tunes.

notation.title: D Dorian Modal Melody
notation.staveTitle: D Dorian - Emphasizing the B Natural (6th)

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Compare D Dorian (with B natural) to D natural minor (with Bb). The B natural gives Dorian its brighter, jazzier quality. Play a Dm chord and alternate between B and Bb to hear the difference clearly.

exercises.title: Mixolydian Rock Vamp
exercises.description: Improvise over an A7 vamp using A Mixolydian (A-B-C#-D-E-F#-G). The characteristic note is G natural (the flat 7th). This is the sound of classic rock, blues-rock, and country. Think 'Sweet Home Alabama' or 'Roadhouse Blues'.

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Mixolydian is like a major scale that rocks. The flat 7th (G instead of G#) gives it that bluesy, dominant quality. Mix in pentatonic licks for an authentic rock sound.

exercises.title: Lydian Dreamy Exploration
exercises.description: Improvise over a Cmaj7 drone using C Lydian (C-D-E-F#-G-A-B). The characteristic note is F# (the sharp 4th). This creates a floating, ethereal quality heard in Joe Satriani's 'Flying in a Blue Dream' and many film scores.

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: The #4 (F#) is what makes Lydian sound 'magical' compared to the regular major scale's F natural. Emphasize this note and let it resolve to the 5th (G) for the quintessential Lydian sound.

exercises.title: Phrygian Dark Tension
exercises.description: Improvise over an Em vamp using E Phrygian (E-F-G-A-B-C-D). The characteristic note is F natural (the flat 2nd). This mode sounds Spanish, Middle Eastern, and heavy - used in flamenco, metal, and prog rock.

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: The b2 interval (E to F, just one fret) creates intense tension. Resolve it back to the root (E) for a dramatic effect. Metallica, Megadeth, and many metal bands use this dark color extensively.

exercises.title: Modal Comparison Exercise
exercises.description: Play a simple 4-bar melody using C Ionian (major), then play the same melodic contour in C Dorian, C Mixolydian, and C Lydian. This trains your ear to hear the unique color each mode provides to the same melodic idea.

notation.title: Same Melody, Different Modes
notation.staveTitle: Modal Color Comparison: Ionian → Dorian → Mixolydian → Lydian

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Each mode changes only 1-2 notes from the major scale, but the emotional impact is dramatic. Record yourself playing each version and listen back to appreciate the different colors.

exercises.title: Modal Chord Vamp Improvisation
exercises.description: Improvise over a two-chord vamp that establishes each mode: Dm7-G7 (Dorian), Em-F (Phrygian), C-D (Lydian), A-G (Mixolydian). The two-chord vamp establishes the modal center without pulling to a traditional resolution.

notation.title: Modal Vamp Progressions
notation.staveTitle: Four Modal Vamps - One Bar Each

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: This is the ultimate modal workout. As you switch vamps, switch your modal focus. The key is emphasizing each mode's characteristic note. Over time, these colors become second nature.

items.title: Developing Modal Awareness
items: Start with one mode per week - immerse yourself in its sound
Listen to songs that feature the mode you're studying
Create your own two-chord vamps as backing tracks
Sing the characteristic note before playing it to internalize the sound

items.title: Modal Music References
items: Lydian: 'Flying in a Blue Dream' (Joe Satriani), 'The Simpsons Theme'
Phrygian: 'Wherever I May Roam' (Metallica), Flamenco music
